commentary_title: Asian demand drives gains in Supramax market as Atlantic rates stabilise
commentary_summary: The Supramax tonne-miles index remained stable in week 42 at 121.1 along with gradual gains across the segment having the Baltic benchmark S10TC rising to $21,539/day. Stronger enquiry and increased Indonesian coal demand supported this sentiment, while the Atlantic remained broadly stable. | The US Gulf benefited from stronger fronthaul enquiry, with petcoke trips to China reaching around $34,000/day. The Continent retained support from grain demand and limited vessel availability, while the Mediterranean showed signs of recovery. The South Atlantic remained steady, with fresh enquiries offering scope for improvement. | The Pacific remained the main source of positive momentum, supported by grain and backhaul cargoes, as well as stronger Indonesian coal demand into India and Bangladesh. Weather-related disruptions across Southeast Asia further constrained vessel availability, with ballast congestion at its peak in the Indian Ocean, allowing owners to maintain firm rate expectations.
